code.qr: QR code for the authenticator app

recovery.file:
{{product}} recovery codes
Each code works once.
recovery.saveBody: If you lose your phone or passkey, each of these codes signs you in once. They are not shown again.

password.label: Password
password.hint: At least 12 characters. A few unrelated words work well.

signIn.title: Sign in to {{product}}
signIn.forgot: Forgot it? Ask an admin for a new password link.
signIn.sessionEnded: Your session ended. Sign in again.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.enterCode: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
mfa.enterRecovery: Enter one of the recovery codes you saved.
mfa.scan: Scan this with an authenticator app (1Password, Bitwarden, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator...).
mfa.enterKey: Enter this key in the app instead:
mfa.required: Owners and admins need a second factor besides the password.

setup.title: Set up {{product}}
setup.withPassword: Create the owner account. You can invite others afterwards.
setup.withProvider: Sign in to become the owner. You can invite others afterwards.
setup.pendingBody: Open the setup link printed in the product's log when it started. Restarting prints a new one.

account.passwordManaged: Kept in {{directory}}. Change it there; you sign in with it here.
account.passwordSignsOut: Changing it signs you out everywhere else.
account.sessionsBody: Where you are signed in. Sign out a session you do not recognise.

members.linkOnce: Send this link to them yourself; it works once, until {{date}}.
members.inviteBody: New members get a link to choose their password. People from an identity provider are linked by their verified email.
members.title: Members
members.alsoMfa: Also remove {{email}}'s second factors? Choose Cancel to keep them.

tokens.newBody: Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. It can do what its role allows in this product only.
tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.label: API tokens
tokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke {{name}}? Anything using it stops working.

providers.badMapping: "{{line}}" must look like group = role, with owner, admin, editor or viewer.
providers.noPkce: {{issuer}} answers, but does not list PKCE with S256, which sign-in uses.
providers.addBody: People sign in through it as well as with passwords and passkeys.
providers.idHint: Part of the redirect URI; it cannot change later.
providers.issuerHint: The address in the provider's discovery document, such as {{example}}
providers.secretHint: Kept encrypted; it is never shown again.
providers.groupsHint: A claim name, or a path such as realm_access.roles.
providers.mappingHint: One group = role per line. With a mapping, groups decide the role on every sign-in and people in none of them are refused.
providers.domainsHint: Comma-separated. For providers where anyone can have an account, such as Google.
providers.showHint: Turned off, nobody can sign in through it, and its settings are kept.
providers.straightHint: The sign-in page opens the provider instead of this product's own form, except after signing out. Add ?local=1 to the address to see the form.
providers.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Nobody can sign in through it any more, and people who did are unlinked from it.
providers.ownersOnlyBody: A role mapping can make anyone in a group an owner, so only owners add, change or remove providers.
providers.title: Identity providers
providers.titleBody: Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google, authentik, ZITADEL, OpenAsy Identity or any OpenID Connect provider.
providers.noneYet: None yet: people sign in with a password or a passkey.
